courses.title: Introduction to Computerized Accounting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Total 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the computer in solving accounting problems. Focuses on the operation of computers. Presents the accounting cycle and financial statement preparation in a computerized system and other applications for financial and managerial accounting.

courses.title: Small Business Taxes
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces taxes most frequently encountered in business. Includes payroll, sales, property, and income tax.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Principles of Accounting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces accounting principles with respect to financial reporting. Demonstrates how decision makers use accounting information for reporting purposes. Focuses on the preparation of accounting information and its use in the operation of organizations, as well as methods of analysis and interpretation of accounting information.

courses.title: Principles of Accounting II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ACC 211
courses.description: Introduces accounting principles with respect to cost and managerial accounting. Focuses on the application of accounting information with respect to product costing, as well as its use within the organization to provide direction and to judge performance.

courses.title: Computerized Accounting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the computer in solving accounting problems. Focuses on operation of computers. Presents the accounting cycle and financial statement preparation in a computerized system and other applications for financial and managerial accounting.

courses.title: Gov't. and Non-Profit Accounting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ACC 212 or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduces fund accounting as used by governmental and nonprofit entities. Stresses differences between accounting principles of for-profit and not-for-profit organizations.

courses.title: Intermediate Accounting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ACC 212 or equivalent.
courses.description: Covers accounting principles and theory, including a review of the accounting cycle and accounting for current assets, current liabilities and investments. Introduces various accounting approaches and demonstrates the effect of these approaches on the financial statement users.

courses.title: Intermediate Accounting II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ACC 221 or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues accounting principles and theory with emphasis on accounting for fixed assets, intangibles, corporate capital structure, long-term liabilities, and investments.

courses.title: Auditing I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite or co-requisite: ACC 212 or equivalent.
courses.description: Presents techniques of investigating, interpreting, and appraising accounting records and assertions. Studies internal control design and evaluation, evidence-gathering techniques and other topics.

courses.title: Prin. of Federal Taxation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the study of federal taxation as it relates to individuals and related entities. Includes tax planning, compliance, and reporting.

courses.title: Prin. of Federal Taxation II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the study of federal taxation as it relates to partnerships, corporations, and other tax entities. Includes tax planning, compliance, and reporting.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Survey of Criminal Justice
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an overview of the United States criminal justice system; introduces the major system components--law enforcement, judiciary, and corrections.

courses.title: The Juvenile Justice System
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the evolution, philosophy, structures and processes of the American juvenile delinquency system; surveys the right of juveniles, dispositional alternatives, rehabilitation methods and current trends.

courses.title: Survey of Criminology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the volume and scope of crime; considers a variety of theories developed to explain the causation of crime and criminality.

courses.title: Introduction to Law Enforcement
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the philosophy and history of law enforcement, presenting an overview of the crime problem and policy response issues. Surveys the jurisdictions and organizations of local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies. Examines the qualification requirements and career opportunities in the law enforcement profession.

courses.title: Law Enforcement Organization & Administration I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite for ADJ 112 , divisional approval or ADJ 111 .
courses.description: Teaches the principles of organization and administration of law enforcement agencies. Studies the management of line operations, staff and auxiliary services, investigative and juvenile units. Introduces the concept of data processing; examines policies, procedures, rules, and regulations pertaining to crime prevention. Surveys concepts of protection of life and property, detection of offenses, and apprehension of offenders. Part I of II.

courses.title: Patrol Procedures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Describes, instructs and evaluates street-level procedures commonly employed by patrol officers in everyday law enforcement operations.

courses.title: Special Enforcement Topics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Considers contemporary issues, problems, and controversies in modern law enforcement.

courses.title: Police Communications and Records
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the principles for the organization and administration of law enforcement communications and records. Examines relationships of custody, central services, and agency logistics to the communications and records operation.

courses.title: Crisis Intervention and Critical Issues
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Addresses basic problems involved in crisis intervention and current critical issues in law enforcement and the administration of justice; emphasizes practical approaches to discover and implement solutions.

courses.title: Introduction to Courts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an overview of the American judiciary--the federal and 50 state judicial systems--with emphasis on criminal court structures, functions, and personnel; surveys the judicial system in Commonwealth of Virginia.

courses.title: Firearms and Marksmanship
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 2-5 hours per week. Prerequisite: Permission of the instructor to enroll. No felony conviction or legal prohibition to possess ammunition of firearms under local, state or federal law.
courses.description: Surveys lethal weapons in current use and current views on weapon types and ammunition design. Examines the legal guidelines as to use of deadly force, safety in handling of weaponry, and weapon care and cleaning; marksmanship instruction under standard range conditions.

courses.title: Patrol Administration and Operations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the goals, methods and techniques of police patrol with focus on the norms which govern work behavior in a police career. Examines the responsibilities of administrators and field supervisors of patrol in the local and state law enforcement agencies.

courses.title: Ethics and the Criminal Justice Professional
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines ethical dilemmas pertaining to the criminal justice system, including those in policing, courts and corrections. Focuses on some of the specific ethical choices that must be made by the criminal justice professional.

courses.title: Collection and Preservation of Physical Evidence
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys fundamental evidence collection procedures, including recognition, selection, handling, packaging and marking. Examines ways to prevent alteration, contamination, damage and tampering. Emphasizes legal requirements for a continuous chain of possession.

courses.title: Defensive Tactics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week. Total 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys and demonstrates the various types of non-lethal force tools and tactics for use by criminal justice personnel in self-defense, arrest, search, restraint and transport of those in custody.

courses.title: Introduction to Corrections
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on societal responses to the offender. Traces the evolution of practices based on philosophies of retribution, deterrence, and rehabilitation. Reviews contemporary correctional activities and their relationships to other aspects of the criminal justice system.

courses.title: Corrections and the Community
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies and evaluates the relationships and interactions between correctional organizations and free society. Focuses on the shared responsibility of the community and corrections agencies to develop effective programs for management and treatment of criminal offenders.

courses.title: Adult Correctional Institutions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Describes the structures, functions, and goals of state and federal correctional institutions (prisons, farms, community-based units, etc.) for adult inmates.

courses.title: Unarmed Security Officers - Duties and Responsibilities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Surveys the theory and practice of un-armed private security personnel duties and responsibilities. Prepares student for licensing and professionalism.

courses.title: Police Response to Critical Incidents
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a basic introduction to incident command and emerging trends. Addresses bomb threats; hostage/barricade situations; attacks on institutions such as schools and hospitals; criminal hazmat; terrorist, militia/paramilitary, and extended crime scene evidence collection scenarios; and other long term or large scale events.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Crime
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a basic introduction to the nature of computer crimes, computer criminals, relevant law, investigative techniques, and emerging trends.

courses.title: Crime Analysis and Intelligence
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a basic introduction to crime analysis and criminal intelligence. covers the need, structure and function within the law enforcement agency, relevant law, and future trends.

courses.title: Case Studies in Murder/Violent Crime
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the student to the investigation of murder and other violent crimes by means of classic case studies and, to the extent feasible, local case files. Includes methodology, strategy and tactics, analysis, relevant law, and future trends. Covers evidentiary techniques and technologies with a primary focus on how critical thinking is applied to serious violent crime.

courses.title: Steet Gangs and Law Enforcement
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the philosophy and history of gangs in America through the eyes of law enforcement, courts, corrections and the citizenry. Examines methods by which law enforcement defines the gang problem and intervenes in gang membership. Explores gang globalization; differentiates street gangs and terrorist cells.

courses.title: Forensic Science I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces student to crime scene technology, procedures for sketching, diagramming and using casting materials. Surveys the concepts of forensic chemistry, fingerprint classification/identification and latent techniques, drug identification, hair and fiber evidence, death investigation techniques, thin-layer chromatographic methods, and arson materials examination. Part I of II.

courses.title: Forensic Science II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces student to crime scene technology, procedures for sketching, diagramming and using casting materials. Surveys the concepts of forensic chemistry, fingerprint classification/identification and latent techniques, drug identification, hair and fiber evidence, death investigation techniques, thin-layer chromatographic methods, and arson materials examination. Part II of II.

courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.

courses.title: On-Site Training
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Specializes in career orientation and training program without pay in selected businesses and industry, supervised and coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Criminology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies current and historical data pertaining to criminal and other deviant behavior. Examines theories that explain crime and criminal behavior in human society.

courses.title: Criminal Law, Evidence and Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the elements of proof for major and common crimes and the legal classification of offenses. Studies the kinds, degrees and admissibility of evidence and its presentation in criminal proceedings with emphasis on legal guidelines for methods and techniques of evidence acquisition. Surveys the procedural requirements from arrest to final disposition in the various American court systems with focus on the Virginia jurisdiction. Part I of II.

courses.title: Criminal Law, Evidence and Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the elements of proof for major and common crimes and the legal classification of offenses. Studies the kinds, degrees and admissibility of evidence and its presentation in criminal proceedings with emphasis on legal guidelines for methods and techniques of evidence acquisition. Surveys the procedural requirements from arrest to final disposition in the various American court systems with focus on the Virginia jurisdiction. Part II of II.

courses.title: Organized Crime and Corruption
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Addresses judicial efforts against and involvement in corruption, drug, vice, and white-collar crimes, both individual and organized.

courses.title: Courts and the Administration of Justice
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ADJ 130 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Studies court systems with emphasis on the technical procedures required, from incident occurrence to final disposition of the case, noting the applicable principles of civil and criminal law; focuses on Virginia courts, laws, and procedures.

courses.title: Constitutional Law for Justice Personnel
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the basic guarantees of liberty described in the U. S. Constitution and the historical development of these restrictions on government power, primarily through U. S. Supreme Court decisions. Reviews rights of free speech, press, assembly, as well as criminal procedure guarantees (to counsel, jury trial, habeas corpus, etc.) as they apply to the activities of those in the criminal justice system.

courses.title: Narcotics and Dangerous Drugs
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the historical and current usage of narcotics and dangerous drugs. Teaches the identification and classification of such drugs and emphasizes the symptoms and effects on their users. Examines investigative methods and procedures utilized in law enforcement efforts against illicit drug usage.

courses.title: Community Policing in Modern Society
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the process through which community problems are identified and addressed by police departments in cooperation with the community. Considers current efforts by law enforcement officers to achieve an effective working relationship with the community.

courses.title: Community Policing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the history of police-community relations and the role of both the community and the police in establishing a crime fighting partnership for success. Emphasizes building relationships between police officers and the community they serve. Includes case studies from various cities that have undertaken the philosophy of community policing.

courses.title: Domestic Violence
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys historical issues that have affected family violence. Examines current trends in the context of the criminal justice system.

courses.title: Terrorism and Counter-Terrorism
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the historical and current practices of terrorism that are national, transnational, or domestic in origin. Includes biological, chemical, nuclear, and cyber-terrorism. Teaches the identification and classification of terrorist organizations, violent political groups and issue-oriented militant movements. Examines investigative methods and procedures utilized in counter terrorist efforts domestically and internationally.

courses.title: Principles of Criminal Investigation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the fundamentals of criminal investigation procedures and techniques. Examines crime scene search, collecting, handling and preserving of evidence.

courses.title: Advanced Criminal Investigation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ADJ 236 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Introduces specialized tools and scientific aids used in criminal investigation. Applies investigative techniques to specific situations and preparation of trial evidence.

courses.title: Techniques of Interviewing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides the student with essential skills and techniques necessary to obtain quality information from victims, witnesses, and suspects, regarding criminal activity. Emphasizes locations and settings for interviews, kinesics, proxemics, and paralinguistics of both the interviewer and interviewee.

courses.title: Correctional Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the legal rights and obligations of the convict- probationer, inmate, and parolee. surveys methods of enforcing both rights and obligations and the responsibilities of corrections agencies and personnel under correctional law (constitutional, statutory, and regulatory provisions).

courses.title: Homeland Security and Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ADJ 111 .
courses.description: Covers relationships abroad, the mission of federal, state, and local government at home, and the best way to provide for the common defense. Examines homeland security and emergency management, the Federal Emergency Management Agency's place in public policy, law, and management, homeland security initiatives, and new partnerships for homeland security covering the government, private sector and higher education. Discusses civil rights issues, the USA Patriot Act; future challenges and roles of intelligence agencies; foreign policy aspects and views.

courses.title: Management of Correctional Facilities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Describes management options and operational implications for staffing, security, safety, and treatment. Considers impact of changes in public policy on corrections.

courses.title: Correctional Counseling
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents concepts and principles of interviewing and counseling as applied in the correctional setting.

courses.title: Criminal Behavior
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces and evaluates the concepts of normal and abnormal behavior. Focuses on the psychological and sociological aspects of criminal and other deviant behavior patterns.

courses.title: Probation, Parole, and Treatment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the philosophy, history, organization, personnel and functioning of traditional and innovative probation and parole programs; considers major treatment models for clients.

courses.title: Counterintelligence Concepts for Law Enforcement and National Security
courses.contact_hours: 3 CreditsLecture Hours: 3Laboratory Hours: 0Total Contact Hours: 3 None
courses.description: Studies the role national security agencies and law enforcement play in counterintelligence programs to identify and thwart hostile criminal activities against United States citizens, businesses, corporations, and U.S. national interests by foreign governments, organizations, and individuals. Focuses on the role of ethical and moral counterintelligence activities and investigations in a democratic society.

courses.title: Firearms and Tool-Mark Identification
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the role of the firearms examiner in forensic science. Teaches the examination techniques and procedures for identifying firearms, tool-marks, ammunition, projectiles and projectile fragments. Instructs on the topics of determining muzzle-to-target distance, gunshot residue tests, firearms nomenclature, comparative micrography, serial number restoration, and the collecting, handling, and presenting of firearms and tool-mark evidence.

courses.title: Capstone Project
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week. Prerequisite: ADJ 236 or equivalent.
courses.description: Provides a capstone research project for the final semester of the program, focusing inquiry upon an area of interest to the student or area relevant to the student's prospective career field. May include problem based research topics, internships, or other focused projects.

courses.description: Covers new content not covered in existing courses in the discipline. Allows instructor to explore content and instructional methods to access the course's viability as a permanent offering.

courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Animal Science and Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the science and technology involved in sustainable animal production and management practices. Includes beef, sheep, horses, dairy, swine, goats, and poultry, with emphasis on practical experiences in laboratory and farm settings.

courses.title: Introduction to Plant Science and Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to plant science, ecology, plant morphology, plant and soil relations and energy conversions. Includes surveying agricultural crops and their importance in the economy.

courses.title: Introduction to Agribusiness and Financial Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours, Laboratory 2-3 hours, Total 4-6 per week. Prerequisite: Local college option.
courses.description: Introduces agriculture's importance to society and ways to start a farm or agribusiness. Evaluates forms of business including cooperatives and create financial statements and reports necessary for routine accounting and tax preparation. Utilizes financial tools for decision making, budgets and time value of money. Explores retirement, transition planning, personal financial management, and capital acquisition techniques.

courses.title: Agriculture Human Resource Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers principles and management practices utilized to attract, retain and motivate agricultural employees. Emphasizes interviewing techniques, employer/employee relationships, motivation theory, legal issues, safety, and environmental concerns. Includes development of team building and interpersonal skills through activities and cases. Explores diversity and cultural differences at they apply to human resource compliance and performance issues.

courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Soil Fertility and Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the factors influencing soil productivity with emphasis upon fertilizer materials from production to application. Discusses time, sources, and soil acidity. Presents soil testing techniques, interpretation of soil tests, and the addition of nutrients to correct or prevent deficiencies.

courses.title: Agribusiness Marketing, Risk Management, and Entrepreneurship
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers marketing techniques required to create an effective marketing plan addressing product, price, place, promotion, and people considerations of an agribusiness. Emphasizes unique aspects of agricultural products and risk management including price fluctuations and biosecurity. Projects explore entrepreneurship and creative marketing plans for a proposed farm or agribusiness.

courses.title: Agricultural Policy, Leadership, and Professional Service
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Enhances personal and professional leadership skills to build consensus and collaboratively solve agricultural issues. Uses the Virginia legislative process to track and influence relevant policy. Partners with stakeholders and key agricultural groups to advocate agriculture's importance to society and remove barriers that prevent farm/agribusiness acquisition and transition. Identifies relevant professional service and leaderships opportunities that will affect changes for the benefit of agricultural and rural communities. Covers current policy and public programs related to taxation, land use, environmental protection, water quality, population changes, water conservation, climate change and quality of rural life. Reinforces written and oral communication skills.

courses.title: Animal Production, Products and Emerging Technologies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches theoretical and practical science-based animal production and management systems; principles of nutrition, reproduction, economics, and breeding and selection of beef cattle, swine, sheep, poultry, goats, fish and other specialty animal enterprises. Includes management practices, marketing, housing, and mitigation of environmental impacts with emphasis on profitable business enterprises for small to medium sized producers and collaborative opportunities to expand profitability for traditional enterprises. Introduces emerging technologies influencing production practices and new products.

courses.title: Duct Construction and Maintenance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents duct materials including sheet metal, aluminum, and fiber glass. Explains development of duct systems, layout methods, safety hand tools, cutting and shaping machines, fasteners and fabrication practices. Includes duct fittings, dampers and regulators, diffusers, heater and air washers, fans, insulation, and ventilating hoods.

courses.title: Air Conditioning and Refrigeration I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies refrigeration theory, characteristics of refrigerants, temperature, and pressure, tools and equipment, soldering, brazing, refrigeration systems, system components, compressors, evaporators, metering devices. Presents charging and evaluation of systems and leak detection. Explores servicing the basic system. Explains use and care of oils and additives and troubleshooting of small commercial systems. Part I of II.

courses.title: Air Conditioning and Refrigeration II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies refrigeration theory, characteristics of refrigerants, temperature, and pressure, tools and equipment, soldering, brazing, refrigeration systems, system components, compressors, evaporators, metering devices. Presents charging and evaluation of systems and leak detection. Explores servicing the basic system. Explains use and care of oils and additives and troubleshooting of small commercial systems. Part II of II.

courses.title: Air Conditioning and Refrigeration III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Psychometric properties of air, heat load and gain calculation, heated and chilled water systems, duct, design, air distribution and air comfort requirements. Part I of II.

courses.title: Air Conditioning and Refrigeration IV
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Psychometric properties of air, heat load and gain calculation, heated and chilled water systems, duct, design, air distribution and air comfort requirements. Part II of II.

courses.title: Circuits and Controls I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 4-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents circuit diagrams for air conditioning units, reading and drawing of circuit diagrams, types of electrical controls. Includes analysis of air conditioning circuits, components, analysis and characteristics of circuits and controls, testing and servicing. Introduces electricity for air conditioning which includes circuit elements, direct current circuits and motors, single and three-phase circuits and motors, power distribution systems, and protective devices. Studies the electron and its behavior in passive and active circuits and components. Demonstrates electronic components and circuits as applied to air conditioning system. Part I of II.

courses.title: Circuits and Controls II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 4-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents circuit diagrams for air conditioning units, reading and drawing of circuit diagrams, types of electrical controls. Includes analysis of air conditioning circuits, components, analysis and characteristics of circuits and controls, testing and servicing. Introduces electricity for air conditioning which includes circuit elements, direct current circuits and motors, single and three-phase circuits and motors, power distribution systems, and protective devices. Studies the electron and its behavior in passive and active circuits and components. Demonstrates electronic components and circuits as applied to air conditioning system. Part II of II.

courses.title: Circuits and Controls III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 4-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces types of circuits and controls used in home, commercial and industrial air conditioning systems. Includes servicing and installation procedures for electrical unloading of compressors, single- and two-stage thermostats, and electrical regulation of fan speed for air volume control. Explains operational and safety control and how schematic and pictorial diagrams are used in these systems.

courses.title: Heating Systems I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces types of fuels and their characteristics of combustion; types, components and characteristics of burners, and burner efficiency analyzers. Studies forced air heating systems including troubleshooting, preventive maintenance and servicing. Part I of II.

courses.title: Heating Systems II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces types of fuels and their characteristics of combustion; types, components and characteristics of burners, and burner efficiency analyzers. Studies forced air heating systems including troubleshooting, preventive maintenance and servicing. Part II of II.

courses.title: Heating Systems III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 3-6 hours week.
courses.description: Introduces types of boilers, sizing boilers, sizing radiators and convectors, designing piping systems for steam, hot water and vacuum systems. Includes testing and servicing wet heat systems.

courses.title: Mechanical Codes
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents mechanical code requirements for installation, service, and inspection procedures . Uses the BOCA code in preparation for the master's card.

courses.title: Heating and Cooling Safety
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Presents standard safety procedures used in the heating and cooling industry. Discusses proper handling of equipment refrigerants and electricity.

courses.title: Air Conditioning Systems I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces comfort survey, house construction, load calculations, types of distribution systems, and equipment selection. Introduces designing, layout, installing and adjusting of duct systems, job costs, and bidding of job. Part I of II.

courses.title: Refrigeration I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4-6 hours. Laboratory 6-9 hours. Total 10-15 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic principles of refrigeration. Includes refrigeration systems, cycles, and use and care of refrigeration tools. Studies shop techniques including soldering, brazing, leak testing, tube testing, tube bending, flaring, and swaging. Analyzes mechanical (vapor compression) systems. Assembles and repairs them including evacuating, charring, testing, and electrical repairs. Introduces advanced troubleshooting and repairs for domestic, commercial and industrial units. Includes medium, low, and ultra low temperature systems of the single and multiple unit types. Includes equipment selection, system balancing, and installation procedures. Part I of II.

courses.title: Planning and Estimating I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents fundamentals of blueprint reading as applied to the building trades. Emphasizes air conditioning distribution, designing and drawing residential and commercial systems, take-off of materials and estimating the cost of the systems. Part I of II.

courses.title: Hydronics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents design and installation of hydronic systems for heating and cooling. Includes steam heated and chilled water systems. Primarily concerns systems using water under forced circulation.

courses.title: Heat Pumps
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies theory and operation of reverse cycle refrigeration including supplementary heat as applied to heat pump systems, including service, installation and maintenance.

courses.title: Advanced Troubleshooting and Service
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents advanced service techniques on wide variety of equipment used in refrigeration, air conditioning, and phases of heating and ventilation and controls.

courses.title: Direct Digital Controls (DDC) I
courses.contact_hours: 3 Credits. Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the principles of direct digital controls. Presents common terms used within the HVAC control industry. Covers the function and operating characteristics of sensors, controllers, and final control devices. Highlights transfer function for a control devise and details the development of equations for typical control transfer functions.

courses.title: Gas Fired Warm Air Furnaces
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: AIR 155 .
courses.description: Covers the study of mid and high efficiency gas-fired warm air furnaces and their components. Includes equipment components, installation, servicing and maintenance.

courses.title: Refrigerant Usage EPA Certification
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Total 1-2 hours per week. Students should have previous training and/or working knowledge of vapor-compression, common service equipment and procedures in HVAC/R.
courses.description: Prepares HVAC technicians for a refrigerant certification test mandated by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Reviews refrigerant recovery, recycle, and reclamation procedures for service work associated with air conditioning and refrigeration. Examines environmental impact including ozone depletion resulting from refrigeration utilization.

courses.title: Beginning Arabic I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning Arabic II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ARA 101 , or two years of successful completion of high school Arabic, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Architectural Drafting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces techniques of architectural drafting, including lettering, dimensioning, and symbols. Requires production of plans, sections, and elevations of a simple building. Studies use of common reference material and the organization of architectural working drawings. Requires development of a limited set of working drawings, including a site plan, related details, and pictorial drawings. Part I of II. Credit will not awarded for both ARC 121 and ARC 123 .

courses.title: Architectural Drafting II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces techniques of architectural drafting, including lettering, dimensioning, and symbols. Requires production of plans, sections, and elevations of a simple building. Studies use of common reference material and the organization of architectural working drawings. Requires development of a limited set of working drawings, including a site plan, related details, and pictorial drawings. Part II of II. Credit will not be awarded for both ARC 122 and ARC 124 .

courses.title: Art Appreciation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces art from prehistoric times to the present day. Describes architectural styles, sculpture, photography, printmaking, and painting techniques. Highlights major artists and key contributions from global and Western culture. Covers content chronologically and/or thematically. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: History of Art: Prehistoric to Gothic
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history and interpretation of architecture, painting and sculpture from the prehistoric era through the Gothic. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: History of Art: Renaissance to Modern
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history and interpretation of architecture, painting and sculpture from the Renaissance through the modern era. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Design for the Web I
courses.contact_hours: Credits - 3. Lecture 2 hours. Studio Instruction - 2 hours. Total Contact - 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic elements of web page design: typography, imagery, and color, and examines how they are combined to create effective layouts. Teaches organization of materials, sketching and concept development, site planning and various methods of construction.

courses.title: Foundations of Drawing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hours. Studio Instruction 4 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops basic drawing skills and understanding of visual language through studio instruction/lecture. Introduces concepts such as line, proportion, space, perspective, value and composition as applied to still life, landscape and figure. Uses drawing media such as pencil, charcoal and ink wash. Includes field trips and gallery assignments as appropriate. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to Painting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Studio instruction 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces study of color, composition and painting techniques. Places emphasis on experimentation and enjoyment of oil and/or acrylic paints and the fundamentals of tools and materials.

courses.title: Introduction to Multimedia
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week. Computer literacy is suggested.
courses.description: Introduces the student to the basic components of multimedia: text, graphics, animation, sound, and video, and explores how they combine to create a multimedia product. Emphasizes the design aspects of multimedia projects and teaches the techniques required to develop a presentation.

courses.title: Two-Dimensional Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Studio instruction 4 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the elements and principles of design as applied to two-dimensional studio projects. Introduces two-dimensional media, techniques, compositional strategies, and color concepts and interactions. Supports conceptual development through introduction to historical and contemporary practices and critical analysis. May include field trips as required. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Three-Dimensional Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Studio instruction 4 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the elements and principles of design as applied to three-dimensional studio projects. Introduces three-dimensional media, techniques, compositional strategies, and color concepts and interactions. Supports conceptual development through introduction to historical and contemporary practices and critical analysis. May include field trips as required. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Time Studio
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Studio instruction 4 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces time-based art concepts and explores the impact of sequence and duration on video, sound, installation, and performance art. Emphasizes the integration of traditional, non-traditional, and emerging production methods and materials in creating time-based artworks.

courses.title: Three Dimensional Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 4 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the concepts of three dimensional design applicable to all fields of Visual Art. Covers tools and techniques. Uses computers as appropriate for research.

courses.title: Ceramics Handbuilding I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-2 hours. Laboratory 4-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces a variety of ceramic handbuilding techniques utilized to design and produce ceramic arts. Includes an introduction to clay, glazes and kilns. Part I of I

courses.title: Ceramics Wheel Throwing I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-2 hours. Laboratory 4-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces a variety of ceramic wheel-throwing techniques utilized to design and produce ceramic arts. Includes an introduction to clay, glazes and kilns. Part I of II.

courses.title: Computer Graphic Techniques
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a working introduction to computer-based electronic technology used by visual artists and designers. Presents the basics of operating platforms and standard industry software. Introduces problems in which students can creatively solve using standard computer graphic applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Art Therapy
courses.contact_hours: Credits - 3. Lecture - 3 hours. Total - 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history of art therapy, contemporary approaches and various settings in which art therapy may occur. Provides instruction in the use of art materials in therapy, dynamics of the creative process, and psychological theory. Reviews educational steps leading to a successful career in art therapy.

courses.title: History of Non-Western Art
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores art as an integral aspect of cultures from Africa, Asia, Islamic groups, Oceania, Native America, and pre-Columbian Central and South America. Increases understanding of the formal and iconographic properties of these works by examining the philosophies, social customs, and ritual practices of their cultures. The assignments in the course require the reading of scholarly articles and researched-based writing.

courses.title: Video Techniques
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Addresses the fundamentals of video technology and non-linear video editing. Focuses on the aesthetics of time-code editing using current industry software. Teaches a student to shoot and capture video and record and edit sound, and combine artwork, animation, video, and sound in the creation of professional-quality original video projects.

courses.title: Painting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Studio instruction 4 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces abstract and representational painting in acrylic and/or oil with emphasis on color, composition, and value.

courses.title: Painting II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Studio instruction 4 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces abstract and representational painting in acrylic and/or oil with emphasis on color, composition, and value. Part II of II.

courses.title: Watercolor I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Studio instruction 2-4 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents abstract and representational painting in watercolor with emphasis on design, color, composition, technique and value. Part I of II.

courses.title: Watercolor II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Studio instruction 2-4 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents abstract and representational painting in watercolor with emphasis on design, color, composition, technique and value. Part II of II.

courses.title: Computer Graphics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Studio instruction 3-4 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Utilizes microcomputers and software to produce computer graphics. Employs techniques learned to solve studio projects which reinforce instruction and are appropriate for portfolio use. Part I of II.

courses.title: Beginning American Sign Language II

courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, comprehension and production skills, and emphasizes basic sentence structure in American Sign Language with a focus on interactive communicative competence. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: History of the U.S. Deaf Community

courses.description: Teaches the alpha/numeric keyboard with emphasis on correct techniques, speed, and accuracy. Teaches formatting of basic personal and business correspondence, reports and tabulation.

courses.title: Keyboarding II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 101 . A laboratory co-requisite (AST 104) may be required.
courses.description: Develops keyboarding and document production skills with emphasis on preparation of specialized business documents. Continues skill-building for speed and accuracy.

courses.title: Editing/Proofreading Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills essential to creating and editing business documents. Covers grammar, spelling, diction, punctuation, capitalization, and other usage problems.

courses.title: Keyboarding for Information Processing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 115) may be required.
courses.description: Teaches the alphabetic and numeric keys: develops correct techniques and competency in the use of computer keyboards. May include basic correspondence and report formats.

courses.title: Keyboarding for Computer Usage
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Teaches the alphabetic keyboard and 10-key pad. Develops correct keying techniques.

courses.title: Word Processing I (Specify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to a word processing program to create, edit, save and print documents.

courses.title: Office Record Keeping
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces types of record keeping duties performed in the office, such as financial, tax, payroll, and inventory. Utilizes specialized software where applicable.

courses.title: Word Processing (Specify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. Prerequisite AST 101 or equivalent. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 144) may be required.
courses.description: Teaches creating and editing documents, including line and page layouts, columns, fonts, search/replace, cut/paste, spell/thesaurus, and advanced editing and formatting features of word processing software.

courses.title: Word Processing II (Specify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 141 or equivalent. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 145) may be required.
courses.description: Teaches advanced software applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Presentation Software (Spcify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces presentation options including slides, transparencies, and other forms of presentations.

courses.title: Desktop Publishing I (Specify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Presents desktop publishing features including page layout and design, font selection, and use of graphic images.

courses.title: Introduction to Call Center Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces concepts and skills needed to be an effective customer service representative for a telephone service operation. Covers call center theory and technology, interpersonal communication skills, customer relations attitudes, telecommunications techniques, and professional procedures to handle a variety of customer service sales requests.

courses.title: Professional Development
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops professional awareness in handling business and social situations. Emphasizes goal setting, critical thinking, decision-making, and employment skills.

courses.title: Microcomputer Office Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 101 or equivalent. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 233) may be required.
courses.description: Teaches production of business documents using word processing, databases, and spreadsheets. Emphasizes document production to meet business and industry standard.

courses.title: Records and Database Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 235) may be required.
courses.description: Teaches filing and records management procedures using microcomputer database software. Incorporates both manual and electronic methods for managing information.

courses.title: Specialized Software Applications (Specify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 101 or equivalent. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 237) may be required.
courses.description: Teaches specialized integrated software application on the microcomputer. Emphasizes document production to meet business and industry standards.

courses.title: Word Processing Advanced Operations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 239) may be required.
courses.description: Teaches advanced word processing features including working with merge files, macros, and graphics; develops competence in the production of complex documents.

courses.title: Medical Insurance and Coding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches coding for medical services rendered within a medical office setting utilizing current coding books for maximum reimbursement.

courses.title: Office Administration I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 101 .
courses.description: Develops an understanding of the administrative support role and the skills necessary to provide organizational and technical support in a contemporary office setting. Emphasizes the development of critical-thinking, problem-solving, and job performance skills in a business office environment.

courses.title: Office Administration II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 243 or equivalent.
courses.description: Enhances skills necessary to provide organizational and technical support in a contemporary office setting. Emphasizes administrative and supervisory role of the office professional. Includes travel and meeting planning, office budgeting and financial procedures, international issues, and career development.

courses.title: Medical Machine Transcription
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 102 or equivalent. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 246) may be required.
courses.description: Develops machine transcription skills, integrating operation of transcribing equipment with understanding of medical terminology. Emphasizes dictation techniques and accurate transcription of medical documents in prescribed formats.

courses.title: Legal Machine Transcription
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 248) may be required. Prerequisite: AST 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Develops machine transcription skills, integrating operation of transcribing equipment with understanding of legal terminology. Emphasizes dictation techniques and accurate transcription of legal documents in prescribed formats.

courses.title: Advanced Desktop Publishing I (Specify Software)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: AST 101 or equivalent and experience in using a word processing package. A laboratory co-requisite (AST 255) may be required.
courses.description: Introduces specific desktop publishing software. Teaches document layout and design, fonts, type styles, style sheets, and graphics.

courses.title: Legal Office Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Co-requisite: AST 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduces general office procedures used in law offices and courts.

courses.title: Medical Office Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Co-requisite: AST 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Covers medical office procedures, records management, preparation of medical reports, and other medical documents.

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces shop practices for automotive laboratory and shop safety, identification and use of hand tools, general power equipment and maintenance of automotive shop. Explains basic operation procedures of standard shop equipment. Presents Occupational Safety and Health Act standards pertaining to the automotive field.

courses.title: Introduction to Automotive Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces fundamental systems of automobile, the engine fuel, exhaust, electric, ignition, lubrication, cooling, transmission, steering, brake and suspension systems. Teaches theory and function of each system. Demonstrates operation.

courses.title: Automotive Engines I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents analysis of power, cylinder condition, valves and bearings in the automotive engine to establish the present condition, repairs or adjustments. Part I of II.

courses.title: Automotive Engines II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents analysis of power, cylinder condition, valves and bearings in the automotive engine to establish the present condition, repairs or adjustments. Part II of II.

courses.title: Automotive Fuel Systems I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyses major domestic and foreign automotive fuel systems to include carburetors and fuel injection systems. Includes detailed inspection and discussion of fuel tanks, connecting lines, instruments, filters, fuel pumps, superchargers, and turbo charger. Also includes complete diagnosis, troubleshooting, overhaul and factory adjustment procedures of all major carbureted and fuel injection systems. Part I of II.

courses.title: Anti-Pollution Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies various anti-pollution systems used on modern automobiles, installation, inspection, repair and service.

courses.title: Introduction to Auto Mechanics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces auto mechanics, covering auto shop safety, tool identification and use. Explains automobile system theory and function. Stresses quality work practices and job opportunities.

courses.title: Automotive Vehicle Inspection
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents information on methods for performing automotive vehicle safety inspection.

courses.title: Auto Power Trains I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents operation, design, construction and repair of power train components, standard and automatic transmission. Includes clutches, propeller shaft, universal joints, rear axle assemblies, fluid couplings, torque converters as well as 2, 3, and 4 speed standard, overdrive and automatic transmissions. Part I of II.

courses.title: Automotive Final Drive and Manual Transmission Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the operation, design, construction and repair of manual transmissions and final drive systems, for both front and rear drive vehicles, including clutches, synchronizers, torque multiplication/gear reduction, along with differentials, transmission/transaxles, drive axels, U-joints, CV joints, 4-wheel drive and all-wheel drive systems.

courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Computerized Fuel Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces devices which sense the engine condition and control fuel mixture to produce economical fuel consumption. Teaches theory of operation, testing, adjustment and repair or replacement of these devices.

courses.title: Introduction to Alternative Fuels and Hybrid Vehicles
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces current trends in alternative fueled vehicles including current alternative fueled vehicles and the implication and safety precautions necessary for working on hybrid vehicles systems.

courses.title: Automotive Heating and Air Conditioning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies separate and combined automotive heaters and air conditioning, including direct and vacuum operated controls, basic principles of refrigeration, adjustment, general servicing, and charging of air conditioning systems.

courses.title: Automotive Electricity I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces electricity and magnetism, symbols and circuitry as applied to the alternators, regulators, starters, lighting systems, instruments and gauges and accessories. Part I of II.

courses.title: Automotive Electricity II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces electricity and magnetism, symbols and circuitry as applied to the alternators, regulators, starters, lighting systems, instruments and gauges and accessories. Part II of II.

courses.title: Automotive Control Electronics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Applied locally
courses.description: Covers the electronic control systems found in hybrid electric vehicle systems, battery electric vehicle systems, and fuel cell electric vehicle systems. Teaches theory, function, and operation of each electronic control system and provides students an opportunity to perform diagnostic procedures and maintenance for these systems. Focuses on safety.

courses.title: Automotive Electronics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 0-3 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces field of electronics as it applies to the modern automobile. Emphasizes basic circuit operation, diagnosis and repair of digital indicator and warning systems.

courses.title: Automatic Transmissions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies several types of automatic transmissions, torque converters, and their principles of operation. Includes adjustment, maintenance, and rebuilding.

courses.title: Automotive Braking Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents operation, design, construction, repair, and servicing of braking system, including Anti-Lock Brake Systems (ABS). Explains uses of tools and test equipment, evaluation of test results, estimation of repair cost for power, standard and disc brakes.

courses.title: Auto Alignment, Suspension and Steering
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 7-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces use of alignment equipment in diagnosing, adjusting, and repairing front and rear suspensions. Deals with repair and servicing of power and standard steering systems.

courses.title: Automotive Suspension and Braking Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the operation, design, construction, repair and servicing of braking and suspension systems. Explains use of tools and test equipment, evaluation of test results, estimation and repair cost, front and rear suspension alignment, power and standard steering, and power, standard and disc brakes.

courses.title: Automotive Driveability and Tune-Up I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents diagnostic and service procedures for automatic electrical and mechanical systems. Teaches use of tools and test equipment, evaluation of test results, estimation of repair cost. Emphasizes performance of required service. Part I of II.

courses.title: Basic Human Biology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents basic principles of human anatomy and physiology. Discusses cells, tissues, and selected human systems.

courses.title: General Biology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on biological processes with a chemical foundation, including macromolecules, cellular structure, metabolism, and genetics in an evolutionary context. Explores the core concepts of evolution; structure and function; information flow, storage and exchange; pathways and transformations of energy and matter; and systems biology. Emphasizes the process of science, interdisciplinary approach, and relevance of biology to society. Part I of a two-course sequence. Assignments require college-level reading fluency, coherent written communication, and basic mathematical skills. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course. Credit toward graduation cannot be awarded for both BIO 101 and BIO 106 .

courses.title: General Biology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: BIO 101 or Departmental Permission
courses.description: Focuses on biological processes with a chemical foundation, including macromolecules, cellular structure, metabolism, and genetics in an evolutionary context. Explores the core concepts of evolution; structure and function; information flow, storage and exchange; pathways and transformations of energy and matter; and systems biology. Emphasizes the process of science, interdisciplinary approach, and relevance of biology to society. Part II of a two-course sequence. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: General Botany
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes plant life cycles, anatomy, morphology, taxonomy, and evolution. Considers the principles of genetics, ecology, and physiology.

courses.title: General Zoology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents basic biological principles, and emphasizes structure, physiology and evolutionary relationships of invertebrates and vertebrates.

courses.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Corequisite or Prerequisite: Demonstration of NAS 2 concepts of Chemical Concepts, Cytology, and Inheritance through NAS 2 completion; or assessment; or module completion; or equivalent.
courses.description: Presents the study of anatomy & physiology including anatomical terminology, homeostasis, histology, integumentary system, skeletal system, muscular system, and nervous system. Part I of II. Assignments require college-level reading fluency, coherent written communication, and basic mathematical skills.

courses.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of BIO 141 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Continues study of anatomy and physiology including endocrine system, blood and cardiovascular system, lymphatic system and immunity, respiratory system, urinary system, fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance, digestive system and nutrient metabolism, reproductive system, and prenatal development. Part II of II.

courses.title: Basic Human Anatomy and Physiology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys human anatomy and physiology. Covers basic chemical concepts, cellular physiology, anatomy, and physiology of human organ systems. Assignments require college-level reading fluency, coherent written communication, and basic mathematical skills.

courses.title: Microbiology for Health Science
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: BIO 101 or BIO 141
courses.description: Focuses on the general characteristics, cellular structure, and metabolism of microorganisms. Emphasizes microbial relationships with individual and community health. Includes impact of microbes on human health and disease, microbial pathogenicity, identifying and managing infectious diseases and controlling microbial growth, healthcare associated infections and epidemiology. Studies aseptic culturing techniques with hands-on experience in safe microbiology practices.

courses.title: Biology for Biotechnology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the student to biological concepts essential to the understanding of biotechnology. Focuses on the structural organization, function, and chemical nature of the cell. Studies cellular processes such as membrane transport, information, processing, reproduction and heredity. Emphasizes laboratory methods of biotechnology.

courses.title: Introduction to Careers in Biotechnology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Exposes the student to the field of biotechnology including skills, opportunities, and employment opportunities. Introduces the requirements to complete training and facilitates the student's need in the construction of a student plan and educational goal.

courses.title: Supervised Study

courses.title: General Microbiology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: ENG 111 , BIO 101 , BIO 102 , and CHM 111 Corequisite: CHM 112
courses.description: Explores the structure and function of microorganisms and their relationship to the environment and humans. Emphasizes the various groups of microorganisms, their growth and metabolism, roles in the functioning of ecosystems, genetics, their roles in human health, the use of microbes in industrial applications and biotechnology and methods of microbial control.

courses.title: Cell Biology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 101 and CHM 111 .
courses.description: Introduces the ultrastructure and functions of cells. Emphasizes cell metabolism, cell division, and control of gene expression.

courses.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 101 , BIO 102 , CHM 111 , and CHM 112
courses.description: Integrates the study of gross and microscopic human anatomy with physiology, emphasizing the analysis and interpretation of physiological parameters, as they relate to clinical scenarios. Covers the integumentary system, skeletal system (including articulations), muscular system, and nervous system. Part I of II.

courses.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: Completion of BIO 231 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Integrates the study of gross and microscopic human anatomy with physiology, emphasizing the analysis and interpretation of physiological parameters, as they relate to clinical scenarios. Covers the endocrine system, circulatory system, lymphatic system (including immunity), respiratory system, urinary system (including fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance), digestive system (including nutrient metabolism), and reproductive system (including prenatal development). Part II of II.

courses.title: Protein Applications in Biotechnology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Prepares students to understand protein structure and function and teaches the laboratory skills needed to successfully work with proteins. Focuses on levels of protein structure and protein function. Includes common laboratory assays will for protein synthesis, purification, detection, and quantification.

courses.title: Nucleic Acid Methods
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides students with advanced laboratory skills needed for employment in the biotechnology industry. Focuses on use of basic and specialized lab equipment and techniques such as solution chemistry, cell culture, DNA extraction and analysis, protein extraction and analysis. Emphasizes lab safety, documentation, quality control, and use of SOPs.

courses.title: General Genetics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 101 & BIO 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Explores the principles of genetics ranging from classical Mendelian inheritance to the most recent advances in the biochemical nature and function of the gene. Includes experimental design and statistical analysis.

courses.title: General Ecology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 101 and BIO 102 .
courses.description: Studies interrelationships between organisms and their natural and cultural environments with emphasis on populations, communities, and ecosystems.

courses.title: Biological Problems in Contemporary Society
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Discusses major biological problems facing society which may include environmental and health concerns such as pollution, bioengineering, drug abuse, conservation, famine and others.
