courses.title: First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the principles and techniques of safety, first aid, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

courses.title: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Provides training in coordinated mouth-to-mouth artificial ventilation and chest compression, choking, life-threatening emergencies, and sudden illness. Equivalent to EMS 100 .

courses.title: Personal and Community Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the basic concepts of health and dimensions of wellness through exploration of a variety of personal health topics. Identifies factors that affect the health status of individuals in addition to health promotion and disease prevention at the personal and community level.

courses.title: Introduction to Personal and Community Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Introduces and focuses on the principles of personal and community health.

courses.title: Introduction to Personal Wellness Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the dimensions of wellness including the physical, emotional, environmental, spiritual, occupational, and social components.

courses.title: Substance Abuse: Prevention and Treatment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the use and abuse of drugs in contemporary society with emphasis upon sociological, physiological, and psychological effects of drugs.

courses.title: Nutrition and Diet Therapy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 0-2 hours. Total 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies nutrients, sources, functions, and requirements with an introduction to diet therapy. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. HLT 230 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Child Health and Nutrition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the physical needs of the preschool child and the methods by which these are met. Emphasizes health routines, hygiene, nutrition, feeding and clothing habits, childhood diseases, and safety as related to health growth and development.

courses.title: Principles of Nutrition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies nutrient components of food, including carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals and water. Provides a behavioral approach to nutrient guidelines for the development and maintenance of optimum wellness. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. HLT 230 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Introduction to Medical Terminology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on medical terminology for students preparing for careers in the health professions. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. HLT 143 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Medical Terminology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of medical abbreviations and terms. Includes the study of prefixes, suffixes, word stems and technical terms with emphasis on proper spelling, pronunciation and usage.

courses.title: Medical Terminology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of medical abbreviations and terms. Includes the study of prefixes, suffixes, word stems, and technical terms with emphasis on proper spelling, pronunciation, and usage. Emphasizes more complex skills and techniques in understanding medical terminology. Part II of II. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. HLT 143 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Ethics for Health Care Personnel
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Total 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on ethical concepts of health care. Emphasizes confidentiality, maintaining patient records, personal appearance, professionalism with patients/clients, associates, and an awareness of health care facilities.

courses.title: Personal Health and Fitness
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the relationships between health and fitness. Topics include nutrition, disease prevention, weight control, smoking and health, medical care, aerobic and anaerobic conditioning, and the relationship between physical and mental health.

courses.title: Introduction to Massage
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Introduces the student to the field of massage therapy. Student practices basic Swedish massage strokes, aromatherapy, effleurage, petrissage and friction, as well as indications and contra-indication for massage.

courses.title: Therapeutic Massage I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 7 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the student to the history and requirements for massage therapy. Covers the terms and practice of massage with introduction to equipment, safety, and ethics as well as massage movements and techniques. Includes information about the benefits of massage, contraindications, client interview, client-therapist relationship, draping, good body mechanics, and anatomical landmarks. Basic massage techniques are blended into a relaxing, health enhancing full-body session preparing the student for their student clinical experience.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Women's Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores current issues related to women's health and wellness with an emphasis upon prevention of disease and optimum well being. Takes a multi-ethnic approach to exploring the most up-to-date findings, diagnostic tools, and treatments for breast cancer, reproductive tract illness, heart, and other common diseases faced by women from puberty through menopause.

courses.title: Workplace Stress Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of the multi-dimensional impacts of stress and its manifestation in the workplace. Explores specific strategies for eliminating, changing and managing stressors in the workplace.

courses.title: Personal Stress Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a basic understanding of stress and explores its physical, psychological and social effects. Includes the relationships among stress and change, self-evaluation, sources of stress, and ways to develop current coping skills for handling stress. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports.

courses.title: Principles of Nutrition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the basic concepts of nutrition and its impact on personal wellness. Emphasizes an evidence-based approach to various topics, such as the nutrient components of food, the components of a healthy eating pattern, and the relationship between diet and health. Provides a behavioral approach to nutrient guidelines for the development and maintenance of optimum wellness. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through documented written reports.

courses.title: Global Health Perspectives
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines global health theories, concepts, issues and prevention efforts. Analyzes the complex relationship between economics, environment, culture and values in addressing health disparities and access to healthcare around the globe. Explores health inequities across the globe by using contemporary, evidence-based topics.

courses.title: General Pharmacology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes general pharmacology for the health related professions covering general principles of drug actions/reactions, major drug classes, specific agent within each class, and routine mathematical calculations needed to determine desired dosages.

courses.title: Basic Pharmacy I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the basics of general pharmacy, reading prescriptions, symbols, packages, pharmacy calculations. Teaches measuring compounds of drugs, dosage forms, drug laws, and drug classifications. Part I of II.

courses.title: Basic Pharmacy II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the basics of general pharmacy, reading prescriptions, symbols, packages, pharmacy calculations. Teaches measuring compounds of drugs, dosage forms, drug laws, and drug classifications. Part II of II.

courses.title: Basic Pharmacy I Lab
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides practical experience to supplement instruction in HLT 261 -262. Should be taken concurrently with HLT 261 -262, in appropriate curricula, as identified by the college. Part I of II.

courses.title: Basic Pharmacy II Lab
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides practical experience to supplement instruction in HLT 261 -262. Should be taken concurrently with HLT 261 -262, in appropriate curricula, as identified by the college. Part II of II.

courses.title: Therapeutic Massage II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 7 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the student to the history and requirements for massage therapy. Covers the terms and practice of massage with introduction to equipment, safety, and ethics as well as massage movements and techniques. Includes information about the benefits of massage, contraindications, client interview, client- therapist relationship, draping, good body mechanics, and anatomical landmarks. Basic massage techniques are blended into a relaxing, health enhancing full-body session preparing the student for their student clinical experience.

courses.title: Therapeutic Massage III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 7 hours per week. Prerequisite: HLT 280 , PTH 151 .
courses.description: Introduces the concept of consultation, client management, session design, and integration of specific therapeutic approaches into a full-body session. Students learn to give specific therapeutic attention to the regions of the back, neck and torso. Using knowledge of muscle anatomy, students perform more advanced massage techniques to address hypertonicity, chronic ischemia, trigger points, fibrotic tissue, adhesions and scar tissue. Includes common clinical applications in the body regions covered and the integration of specific techniques into a full-body session.

courses.title: Introduction to Human Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces human service agencies, roles and careers. Presents an historical perspective of the field as it relates to human services today. Additional topics include values clarification and needs of target populations.

courses.title: Working With Death and Dying
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the hospice concept emphasizing the management of providing services associated with terminal illness, while providing human services for the family as well as the patient. Explores the unique role of each member of the hospice care team as to how each assists the patient and family in coping with the effects of the illness. Emphasizes understanding grief and loss. Focuses on the dying person and emphasizes the social and moral aspects of death and dying.

courses.title: Basic Counseling Skills I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills needed to function in a helping relationship. Emphasizes skills in attending, listening and responding. Clarifies personal skill strengths, deficits and goals for skill improvement.

courses.title: Community Resources and Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies federal, state, and local agencies, their functions, limitations and interrelationships. Emphasizes purposes of agencies as related to delivery of human services and procedures for referral, team building, and regional cooperation.

courses.title: Group Dynamics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the stages of group development, group dynamics, the role of the leader in a group, and recognition of the various types of group processes. Discusses models of group dynamics that occur as a result of group membership dynamics.

courses.title: Group Dynamics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines group dynamics, group leadership, group cohesion, transference and group helping through experiential involvement in group facilitating and leadership. Increases group skills through active classroom participation in group experiences.

courses.title: Effects of Psychoactive Drugs
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides information on the biochemical, physiological, and behavioral aspects of substance addiction and will review the symptoms of addiction. Emphasizes areas of chemical dependency, medical epidemiology, physiological threats of addiction and methods of identifying multiple drug abusers.

courses.title: Professional Skill Development for Human Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teach professional skills necessary to make the transition from the role of MH consumer/client to that of services provider. Will cover confidentiality, professionalism, boundaries and roles, cultural diversity and personal values.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Addiction and Prevention
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the impact of drugs and addiction on individuals and their families. Explores the myths about various drugs and their benefit or lack of benefit.

courses.title: Functional Family Intervention
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of functions and dysfunctions within the family. Emphasizes the development of effective skills through an interpersonal/interactional approach to family intervention.

courses.title: Helping Across Cultures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an historical overview of selected cultural and racial groups. Promotes understanding of group differences and the impact on counseling services.

courses.title: The Helper As a Change Agent
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the following skills for implementing alternative models of change and influence: action research, problem- solving, consultation, workshop development, and outreach and advocacy for diverse client populations.

courses.title: Productive Problem-Solving
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops problem-solving and program-development skills needed to function in helping relationships. Emphasizes skills-training within the classroom and application of the skills in other settings.

courses.title: Gerontology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the process of aging; its implications in relation to health, recreation, education, transportation, meaningful work or activity, and to community resources. Emphasizes experiencing the aging process, facilitating retirement, and application of the helping relationship to work with older adults.

courses.title: Principles of Case Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of current case management theory and practice in the field of mental health.

courses.title: Substance Use Treatment I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides knowledge, skills, and insight for working in substance use programs. Emphasizes personal growth and client growth measures in helping relationships. Stresses various methods of individual and group techniques for helping the individual with substance use disorder.

courses.title: Substance Use Treatment II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: HMS 251 .
courses.description: Expands knowledge and skill in working with individuals with substance use disorder. Focuses on assisting people with substance use disorder in individual and group settings and explores client treatment modalities. May provide opportunities for field experience in treatment centers.

courses.title: Case Management and Substance Abuse
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the process for interviewing substance abuse clients. Includes intake, assessment, handling denial, and ending the interview. Teaches skills for writing short-term goals and treatment plans with emphasis on accountability. Examines various reporting devices.

courses.title: Substance Abuse Counseling
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of the skills of guidance of clients and those associated with being an advocate. Examines the dynamics of the client/counselor relationship in developing treatment plans and empowerment skills.

courses.title: Human Behavior I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills in working with individuals, families, groups, organizations and communities within the socio- cultural context. Emphasizes historical development of various social systems and how these systems affect the whole person. Part I of II.

courses.title: Personality Theory
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the theories of personality and their relationship to counseling. Emphasis is on the historical perspective, view of human nature, contributions and limitations of each theory.

courses.title: Counseling Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies major counseling theories, their contributions and limitations, and the application of each to a counseling interaction. Students develop their own personal counseling theory.

courses.title: Treatment Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the services and facilities established for the purpose of treating addictions. Focuses on treatment therapy models and ethical standards related to addiction-disease theory.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Hotel-Restaurant Organization and Management I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history, opportunities, problems and trends of the hospitality industry. Covers the organization of the various sectors of the hospitality industry including human resources, general business considerations, and management theory. Part I of II.

courses.title: Hotel-Restaurant Organization and Management II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history, opportunities, problems and trends of the hospitality industry. Covers the organization of the various sectors of the hospitality industry including human resources, general business considerations, and management theory. Part II of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Culinary Arts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Covers the historical perspective of the cooking and hospitality industry. Includes career paths and opportunities for culinarians, culinary professionalism, people skills, motivational and organizational skills.

courses.title: Principles of Culinary Arts I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of food preparation and basic culinary procedures. Stresses the use of proper culinary procedures combined with food science, proper sanitation, standards of quality for food items that are made, and proper use and care of kitchen equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Principles of Culinary Arts I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of food preparation and basic culinary procedures. Stresses the use of proper culinary procedures combined with food science, proper sanitation, standards of quality for food items that are made, and proper use and care of kitchen equipment. Part II of II.

courses.title: Food Service Managers Sanitation Certification
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Presents an accelerated survey of principles and applications of sanitary food service, designed to promote the skills of managers in food service establishments licensed by the Commonwealth of Virginia. (Upon successful completion of the course, a certificate of achievement is awarded by the Educational Foundation of the National Restaurant Association and the student's name is entered in the Foundation Registry.)

courses.title: Principles of Food Preparation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies scientific principles and techniques to the preparation of food, including carbohydrates, such as fruits, vegetables, sugars and starches; fats, including both animal and vegetable, as well as natural and manufactured; and proteins, such as milk, cheese, eggs, meats, legumes, fish and shellfish.

courses.title: The Art of Garnishing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the relationship between colors and shapes and how they pertain to garnishes. Provides student with knowledge to create impressive presentations.

courses.title: Principles of Baking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Instructs the student in the preparation of breads, pastries, baked desserts, candies, frozen confections, and sugar work. Applies scientific principles and techniques of baking. Promotes the knowledge/skills required to prepare baked items, pastries and confections.

courses.title: Food and Beverage Service Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a conceptual and technical framework for managing the service of meals in a variety of commercial settings. Studies the integration of production and service delivery, guest contact dynamics, reservations management and point-of-sale systems.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Quality for the Hospitality Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches quality in the hospitality industry, including material on the total quality management movement. Emphasizes quality from the customer's perspective.

courses.title: Sanitation and Safety
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers the moral and legal responsibilities of management to insure a sanitary and safe environment in a food service operation. Emphasizes the causes and prevention of foodborne illnesses in conformity with federal, state and local guidelines. Focuses on OSHA standards in assuring safe working conditions.

courses.title: Executive Housekeeping
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the housekeeping department with emphasis on organization, staffing and scheduling, staff development, work methods improvements, equipment, cleaning materials and cleaning procedures; maintenance and refurnishing; room design and safety engineering.

courses.title: Convention Management and Service
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the scope and different segments that make up the convention market; explains what is required to meet individual needs; and explores methods and techniques for better service.

courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Hotel Front Office Operations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes hotel front office positions and the procedures involved in reservation registration, accounting for and checking out guests, and principles and practices of night auditing. Covers the complete guest operation in both traditional and computerized operations.

courses.title: Introduction to Food Service Assisting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies food service assisting and responsibilities, cooking terminology, as well as techniques and procedures. Identifies equipment and utensils. Covers measurement equivalents. Reviews fractions. Studies hygiene, sanitation, and safety standards.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Practical Horticulture
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides practical experience in landscape construction equipment operations and maintenance.

courses.title: Principles of Horticulture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces concepts of plant growth and development. Covers horticultural practices, crops and environmental factors affecting plant growth.

courses.title: Horticultural Botany
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies taxonomy, anatomy, morphology, physiology, and genetics of plants as applied to identification, propagation and culture.

courses.title: Applied Mathematics for the Green Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers the basic math skills needed in the Green Industry to include areas, volumes, calibration calculations, profit and loss statements, and topics specific to turf, landscape, greenhouse, nursery, and interior landscapes.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: On-Site Training
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Specializes in career orientation and training program without pay in selected businesses and industry, supervised and coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Landscape Plants I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies landscape use of plants. Considers ornamental value, growth habit, identification, and limitations. Part I of II.

courses.title: Soils
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches theoretical and practical aspects of soils and other growing media. Examines media components, chemical and physical properties, and soil organisms. Discusses management and conservation.

courses.title: Planting Design I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies landscape theory and principles of drawing to the planning of residential and small scale commercial landscape designs.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Great Books I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces selected great works of philosophy and literature, with emphasis on close analysis of the text. Part I of II.

courses.title: Great Books II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces selected great works of philosophy and literature, with emphasis on close analysis of the text. Part II of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Appalachian Studies
courses.contact_hours: Course Credits 3, Lecture 3
courses.description: Explores the Appalachian region from a cross-disciplinary perspective, with readings on Appalachia drawn primarily from the humanities. Considers the historical, environmental, political and economic contexts that shape Appalachia.

courses.title: Controversial Issues in Contemporary American Culture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to selected issues in contemporary American culture. Includes topic areas ranging from welfare reform, economic development, privacy, environmental protection and conservation, evolution vs. creation, to family values, and special interest lobbying in our state and national governments. Focuses on the development of the student's critical thinking skills by analyzing, evaluating, and reflecting on opposing sides of the same issue as expressed by public leaders, special interest groups and academicians.

courses.title: Studies In
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours per week.
courses.description: Covers new content not covered in existing courses in the discipline. Allows instructor to explore content and instructional methods to assess the course's viability as a permanent offering.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Early Humanities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the values and expression of ideas of selected western and non-western cultures from prehistory up to the 1300s, integrating the arts, literature, religion, and philosophy within the context of history. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Modern Humanities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the values and expression of ideas of selected western and non-western cultures from the 1300s until 1900s, integrating the visual arts, literature, religion, music and philosophy within the context of history. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to Women and Gender Studies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Broadens understanding and awareness of women by exploring different cultural, historical, and gendered experiences of social groups throughout the world in relationship to such fields as art, literature, religion, philosophy, social sciences, and music. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Native American Culture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the cultural history of Native (Indian) peoples in the Americas from the pre-Columbian era until the present. Studies history, religion, literature, arts, life-ways and world-views which comprise the diverse traditions of Native peoples.

courses.title: Introduction to Non-Western Cultures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to beliefs, historical developments, and forms of creative expression that have shaped cultures in regions outside Europe and North America (non-western). Studies the cultures, values, creative expressions, and historical development of selected non-western regions of the world: Asia, Africa, Middle East, Oceania, or the Pre-Columbian Americas. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Survey of Horror
courses.contact_hours: (3 Cr.) Lecture 3 hours, Total 3 hours per week Fluency in Standard American English. Recommend proficiency in reading and writing at English 111 level
courses.description: Surveys and analyzes the horror genre, focusing on the psychological, anthropological, and historical background of monsters. Acquaints students with recurring horror themes in literature, art, and popular culture from around the world.

courses.title: Introduction to African American Studies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an interdisciplinary approach to the study of African-American life, history, and culture. Examines specific events, ideologies, and individuals that have shaped the contours of African-American life. Studies the history, sociology, economics, religion, politics, psychology, creative productions, and culture of African- Americans. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Creative Thinking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines, analyzes, and develops creative and critical thinking processes with individual and group applications to solve business, scientific, social, environmental, and other practical problems. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports.

courses.title: Comparative Mythology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the cultural expressions of mythology. Considers selected mythologies representing diverse global culture, with emphasis on parallels and divergences in structure, purpose, and representation in literature and the arts. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.description: Examines selected values and expressions of ideas of western and non-western cultures throughout the twentieth century and beyond, integrating the visual arts, literature, performing arts, religion, and philosophy within the context of history. courses.title: Materials and Processes of Industry

courses.description: Studies materials and processes for the manufacture of products. Investigates the nature of various materials. Examines the manufacturing processes of industry and their effects on materials.

courses.title: Industrial Supervision I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the concept of the Supervisor as a Leader. Discusses the role of the Industrial Supervisor in the face of technology advances. Discusses the role of the Industrial Supervisor in leading organizational change and helping employees through transitions. Defines Leadership styles and the selection of the appropriate style. Introduces the Industrial Supervisor as a motivator in terms of job satisfaction, morale, job design competition, communication, and promotions. Presents ethical behavior and dilemmas in organizations.

courses.title: Team Concepts & Problem Solving
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies team concepts and problem solving techniques to assist project teams in improving quality and productivity. Provides knowledge of how to work as a team, plan and conduct good meetings, manage logistics and details, gather useful data, communicate the results and implement changes.

courses.title: Industrial Leadership and Career Development
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour, Total 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Covers the importance of effective and ethical organizational behavior in career development. Provides students with guidance on how to be a high performance team member. Presents the tools necessary to manage and motivate team members in a manufacturing environment. Focuses on communication skills, professionalism, and ethics. Examines conflict resolution skills and the ability to identify behavioral types.

courses.title: Quality Control
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies history, structure, and organization of the quality control unit. May include incoming material control, product and process control, and cost control.

courses.title: Workplace Ethics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Provides a broad overview of ethics in the modern day business world including workforce skill building and self awareness through group discussions. Discusses workplace topics such as diversity, substance abuse, hiring and firing and workplace practices, appropriate dress, communication, business ethics, and interviewing.

courses.title: Introduction to Robotics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 0-2 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies evolution and history of robotics with an emphasis on automated and flexible manufacturing. Presents advantages and limitations of present robot systems.

courses.title: Principles of Industrial Technology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week.`
courses.description: Introduces principle concepts of technology involving mechanical, fluid, electrical, and thermal power as they relate to force, work, and rate.

courses.description: Introduces principle concepts of technology involving mechanical, fluid, electrical, and thermal power as they relate to resistance, energy, power, and force transformers. Places an emphasis on mechanical and advantage systems.

courses.title: Introduction to Basic Computer Integrated Manufacturing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3-9 hours. Total 4-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents basic principles used in the design and implementation in a computer integrated manufacturing system. Emphasizes team concept and all aspects of a computer integrated manufacturing system to include the following: Robotics, Conveyor Control, Machining Center Integration Quality Control, Statistical Quality Control, and Computer Integrated Manufacturing (CIM) software.

courses.title: Web Page Design I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Stresses a working knowledge of web site designs, construction, and management using HTML or XHTML. Includes headings, lists, links, images, image maps, tables, forms, and frames.

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the creation of digital graphics for web design. Includes basic design elements such as color and layout will be explored utilizing a computer graphics program(s).

courses.title: Design Concepts for Mobile Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides skills for designing both Web-based and stand-alone applications for wireless devices. Details discussions of the needs for applications including mobile phones and a range of rich hand-held devices such as PDA's. Emphasizes the importance of usability, accessibility, optimization and performance to create fast-loading business enterprise applications and games.

courses.title: Database Fundamentals
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the student to Relational Database and Relational Database theory. Includes planning, defining and using a database; table design, linking, and normalization; types of databases, database description and definition.

courses.title: Database Management Software
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers an introduction to relational database theory and how to administer and query databases using multiple commercial database systems.

courses.title: Web Page Design II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Incorporates advanced techniques in web site planning, design, usability, accessibility, advanced site management, and maintenance utilizing web editor software(s).

courses.title: Interactive Web Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides techniques in interactive design concepts to create cross-platform, low-bandwidth animations utilizing a vector based application. Emphasizes the importance of usability, accessibility, optimization and performance.

courses.title: Database Architecture and Administration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Involves in-depth instruction about the underlying architecture of databases and the handling of database administration.

courses.title: Introduction to Microcomputers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines concepts and terminology related to microcomputers and introduces specific uses of microcomputers.

courses.title: Computers and Information Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces terminology, concepts, and methods of using computers in information systems. This course teaches computer literacy, not intended for Information Technology majors.

courses.title: Careers and Cyber Ethics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Career paths in Information Technology will be explored to help the student determine the appropriate degree plan. Career paths will include but not be limited to software development, computer science, database, networking, system administration and operations, end user support, web design, and management. The student will learn ethical concerns in business and information technology including the ACM Code of Ethics.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Applications and Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers computer concepts and internet skills, and uses a software suite which includes word processing, spreadsheet, database, and presentation software to demonstrate skills. Recommended prerequisite keyboarding skills. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. ITE 152 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Survey of Computer Software Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Review current business software applications for microcomputers emphasizing comparison of a variety of software packages. Provides experience with multiple operating system commands, database, spreadsheet, and word processing programs.

courses.title: Information Literacy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the information literacy core competencies focusing on the use of information technology skills. Skills and knowledge will be developed in database searching, computer applications, information security and privacy, and intellectual property issues. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. ITE 152 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Introduction to Internet Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides students with a working knowledge of Internet terminology and services including e-mail, WWW browsing, search engines, ftp, file compression, and other services using a variety of software packages. Provides instruction for basic web page construction.

courses.title: Survey of Internet Services

courses.description: Introduces students to basic Internet terminology and services including e-mail, WWW browsing, search engines, ftp telnet, and other services.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence Awareness
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in the basics of artificial intelligence (AI) including the complexities of AI, machine and deep learning, and neural networks. Provides students with a clear understanding of history, terminology, concepts, and mechanisms driving AI technologies. Explores how AI is applied in various occupational fields through a blend of theoretical knowledge and case studies.

courses.title: Spreadsheeting for Business
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a working knowledge of a commercial spreadsheet package to include design and development of a variety of worksheets, preparing graphs, working with database queries, macro writing, menu techniques, and decision analysis tools.

courses.title: Microcomputer Software: Spreadsheets
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides first-time users with sufficient information to make practical use of spreadsheet software using the basic of building spreadsheets.

courses.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence Tools for Business
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the applications of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in business. Studies how AI can enhance efficiency, optimize decision-making, and drive innovation in business environments. Includes hands-on projects using AI tools and platforms.

courses.title: Desktop Database Software
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Incorporates instruction in planning, defining, and using a database; performing queries; producing reports; working with multiple files; and concepts of database programming. Includes database concepts, principles of table design and table relationships, entering data, creating and using forms, using data from different sources, filtering, creating mailing labels.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital and Information Literacy and Computer Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops understanding of digital and information literacy. Introduces basic computer concepts in hardware, software, cyber, cloud, database, and operating systems. Includes hands-on experience developing word processing, spreadsheet and presentation documents. Evaluates the reliability of sources. Covers creating a simple web page. Examines topics such as social, legal, and ethical issues. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to E-Commerce
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the culture and demographics of the Internet, on-line business strategies and the hardware and software tools necessary for Internet commerce. Includes the identification of appropriate target segments, the development of product opportunities, pricing structures, distribution channels over the Internet, and the execution of marketing strategy in computer- mediated environments. Presents case histories of successful Web applications.

courses.title: Multimedia Software
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores technical fundamentals of creating multimedia projects with related hardware and software. Students will learn to manage resources required for multimedia production and evaluation and techniques for selection of graphics and multimedia software.

courses.title: Email Essentials
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on providing the student with a working knowledge of introductory email function. Includes the basic concepts of customizing email and using all the email capabilities for reading, creating, sending emails, managing calendar functions and managing contacts, tasks, and notes.

courses.title: Help Desk Support Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes instruction in customer support techniques required for analyzing and coordinating software and hardware solutions for end-user needs. includes evaluation and communication techniques required to provide help desk support necessary to transfer knowledge and enable implementation of a solution.

courses.title: User Support/Help Desk Principles
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces a variety of tools and techniques that are used to provide user support in help desk operations. courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys data transmission systems, communication lines, data sets, network, modes of transmission, protocols, and interfacing. Emphasizes network structure and operation.

courses.title: Introduction to Network Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in networking media, physical and logical topologies, common networking standards and popular networking protocols. Emphasizes the TCP/IP protocol suite and related IP addressing schemes, including CIDR. Includes selected topics in network implementation, support and LAN/WAN connectivity.

courses.title: Administration of Networked Servers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Instruction focuses on the installation, configuration, and management of local area networked servers. Topics covered include support for local area networked devices, system services, and deployment of networked operating systems. This course can include any version of Windows or Linux Server Platforms.

courses.title: Microcomputer Operating Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches use of operating system utilities and multiple-level directory structures, creation of batch files, and configuration of microcomputer environments. May include a study of graphical user interfaces.

courses.title: Personal Computer Hardware and Troubleshooting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes specially designed instruction to give a student a basic knowledge of hardware and software configurations. Includes the installation of various peripheral devices as well as basic system hardware components.

courses.title: Internet and Network Foundation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Laboratory 0-2 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a basic comprehension of Internet and network technologies including IT job roles, connection methods, TCP/IP functionality and DNS. Explores web server technologies with security and project management concepts. Introduces network creation, physical and logical topologies including media properties, server types, IP addressing and network security.

courses.title: Client Operating System (Specify Version)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers installation, configuration, administration, management, maintenance, and troubleshooting of the desktop client operating system in a networked environment.

courses.title: Server Administration (Specify Version)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers installation, configuration, administration, management, maintenance, and troubleshooting of a server in a networked environment.

courses.title: Network Infrastructure (Specify Version)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers planning, installation, configuration, administration, management, maintenance, monitoring, and troubleshooting of network infrastructure components.

courses.title: Introduction to Networks - Cisco
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in the fundamentals of networking environments, the basics of router operations, and basic router and switch configuration.

courses.title: Switching, Routing and Wireless Essentials - Cisco
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITN 154
courses.description: Provides the skills and knowledge to install, operate, and troubleshoot routers and switches in small networks. Introduces students to wireless local area networks (WLANS) and network security concepts.

courses.title: Enterprise Networking, Security, and Automation - Cisco
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITN 155
courses.description: Teaches students to configure, troubleshoot, and secure enterprise networks. Introduces students to virtualization, application programming interfaces (APIs) and the configuration management tools that make network automation possible.

courses.title: WAN Technologies - Cisco
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Concentrates on an introduction to Wide Area Networking (WANs). Includes WAN design, LAPB, Frame Relay, ISDN, HDLC, and PPP.

courses.title: Linux System Administration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses instruction on the installation, configuration and administration of the Linux operating system and emphasizes the use of Linux as a network client and workstation.

courses.title: Unix 1
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to UNIX operating systems. Teaches login procedures, file creation, UNIX file structure, input/output control, and the UNIX shell.

courses.description: Focuses on advanced storage systems, protocol, and architectures including Storage Area Networks (SAN), Network Attached Storage (NAS), Fibre Channel Networks, Internet Protocol SANs (IPSAN), iSCSI, and Content Addressable Storage (CAS).

courses.title: Cloud Computing: Infrastructure and Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on cloud infrastructure, deployment, security models, and the key considerations in migrating to cloud computing. Covers the technologies and processes required to build traditional, virtualized, and cloud data center environments, including computation, storage, networking, desktop and application virtualization, business continuity, security, and management.

courses.title: Network Security Basics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in the basics of network security in depth. Includes security objectives, security architecture, security models and security layers; risk management, network security policy, and security training. Includes the five security keys, confidentiality integrity, availability, accountability and auditability.

courses.title: Network Attacks, Computer Crime and Hacking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Encompasses in-depth exploration of various methods for attacking and defending a network. Explores network security concepts from the viewpoint hackers and their attack methodologies. Includes topics about hackers, attacks, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) malicious code, computer crime and industrial espionage.

courses.title: Network Communication, Security and Authentication
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers an in-depth exploration of various communication protocols with a concentration on TCP/IP. Explores communication protocols from the point of view of the hacker in order to highlight protocol weaknesses. Includes Internet architecture, routing, addressing, topology, fragmentation and protocol analysis, and the use of various utilities to explore TCP/IP.

courses.title: Internet/Intranet Firewalls and E-Commerce Security
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Gives an in-depth exploration of firewall, Web security, and e-commerce security. Explores firewall concepts, types, topology and the firewall's relationship to the TCP/IP protocol. Includes client/server architecture, the Web server, HTML and HTTP in relation to Web Security, and digital certification, D.509, and public key infrastructure (PKI).

courses.title: Network Security Layers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an in-depth exploration of various security layers needed to protect the network. Explores Network Security from the viewpoint of the environment in which the network operates and the necessity to secure that environment to lower the security risk to the network. Includes physical security, personnel security, operating system security, software security and database security.

courses.title: Legal Topics in Network Security
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours hours per week.
courses.description: Conveys an in-depth exploration of the civil and common law issues that apply to network security. Explores statutes, jurisdictional, and constitutional issues related to computer crimes and privacy. Includes rules of evidence, seizure and evidence handling, court presentation and computer privacy in the digital age.

courses.title: Computer Forensics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITN 106 , ITN 107 . Co-requisite: ITN 260 .
courses.description: Teaches computer forensic investigation techniques for collecting computer-related evidence at the physical layer from a variety of digital media (hard drives, compact flash and PDAs) and performing analysis at the file system layer. Credit will be given to ITN 275 or ITN 276 and ITN 277 , but not all three courses.

courses.description: Concentrates instruction in fundamentals of object-oriented programming using Visual Basic.NET and the .NET framework. Emphasizes program construction algorithm development, coding debugging, and documentation of graphical user interface applications.

courses.title: Java Programming I

courses.description: Entails instruction in fundamentals of object-oriented programming using Java. Emphasizes program construction, algorithm development, coding, debugging, and documentation of console and graphical user interface applications.

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents instruction in fundamentals of object-oriented programming and design using C#. Emphasizes program construction, algorithm development, coding, debugging, and documentation of applications within the .NET framework.

courses.title: Client Side Scripting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in fundamentals of Internet application design, development, and deployment using client side scripting language(s).

courses.title: Python Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Entails instruction in fundamentals of object-oriented programming using Python. Emphasizes program construction, algorithm development, coding, debugging, and documentation of Python applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Game Design & Development
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces object-oriented game design and development. Provides overview of the electronic game design and development process and underlines the historical contest, content creation strategies, game careers, and future trends in the industry. Utilizes a game language environment to introduce game design, object-oriented paradigms, software design, software development and product testing. Teaches skills of writing a game design document and creating a game with several levels and objects. Integrate 2D animations, 3D models, sound effects, and background music as well as graphic backgrounds.

courses.title: Project Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the concepts of project management as defined by the Project Management Institute, the accreditation body for project management.

courses.title: Concepts of Programming Languages
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents instruction in the fundamental concepts of computer programming languages. Emphasis on architectural reasons behind programming language constructs. Provides a getter understanding of how and why programming languages work the way they do.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Java Programming II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Imparts instruction in application of advanced object-oriented techniques to application development using Java. Emphasizes database connectivity, inner classes, collection classes, networking, and threads.

courses.title: Web Scripting Languages
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisites: ITD 110 , ITP 100 .
courses.description: Introduces students to the principles, systems, and tools used to implement Web applications. Provides students with a comprehensive introduction to the programming tools and skills required to build and maintain interactive Web sites. Students will develop Web applications utilizing client-side and server-side scripting languages along with auxiliary tools needed for complete applications.

courses.title: C++ Programming II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents in-depth instruction of advanced object-oriented techniques for data structures using C++.

courses.title: Developing User Interfaces
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in the creation of computer application user interfaces that offer intuitive navigation and informative design for web, mobile, and desktop applications, and other technologies.

courses.title: Beginning Japanese I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning Japanese II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: JPN 101 , or two years of successful completion of high school Japanese, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Real Estate Law for Legal Assistants
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies law of real property and gives in-depth survey of the more common types of real estate transactions and conveyances such as deeds, contracts, leases, and deeds of trust. Focuses on drafting these various instruments and studies the system of recording and search of public documents.

courses.title: Family Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies elements of a valid marriage, grounds for divorce and annulment, separation, defenses, custody, support, adoptions, and applicable tax consequences. Includes property settlement agreements, pre- and ante-nuptial agreements, pleadings, and rules of procedure. May include specific federal and Virginia consumer laws.

courses.title: Legal Research and Writing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 111 or permission of division.
courses.description: Provides a basic understanding of legal research and the proper preparation of legal documents, including brief writing.

courses.title: Estate Planning and Probate
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces various devices used to plan an estate, including wills, trust, joint ownership and insurance. Considers various plans in light of family situations and estate objectives. Focuses on practices involving administration of an estate including taxes and preparation of forms.

courses.title: Legal Aspects of Business Organizations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies fundamental principles of agency law and the formation of business organizations. Includes sole proprietorships, partnerships, corporation, limited liability companies, and other business entities. Reviews preparation of the documents necessary for the organization and operation of businesses.

courses.title: Numerical Control I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on numerical control techniques in metal forming and machine processes. Includes theory and practice in lathe and milling machine computer numerical control program writing, setup and operation. Part I of II.

courses.title: Numerical Control II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on numerical control techniques in metal forming and machine processes. Includes theory and practice in lathe and milling machine computer numerical control program writing, setup and operation. Part II of II.

courses.title: Computer Numerical Control III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on numerical control techniques in metal forming and machine processes. Includes theory and practice in lathe and milling machine computer numerical control program writing, setup and operation.

courses.title: Introductory CNC Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces programming of computerized numerical control machines with hands-on programming and operation of CNC machines.

courses.title: Advanced CNC Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides in-depth study of programming computerized numerical control machines.

courses.title: CNC Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches programming of computerized numerical control machines. Focuses on CNC machining processes.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Aided Manufacturing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces computer aided manufacturing (CAM) with emphasis on programming of numerical control machinery. Teaches program writing procedures using proper language and logic and a CAM programming system to produce numerical control code for machines. Teaches basic computer usage, 2 1/2D and 3D CAD-CAM integration, and code-to-machine transfer.

courses.title: Machine Tool Maintenance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces tool design from a maintenance and repair standpoint. Emphasizes proper care, repair, and preventative maintenance of machine tools.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces safety procedures, bench work, hand tools, precision measuring instruments, drill presses, cut-off saws, engine lathes, manual surface grinders, and milling machines. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces safety procedures, bench work, hand tools, precision measuring instruments, drill presses, cut-off saws, engine lathes, manual surface grinders, and milling machines. Part II of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers practice in the operation of the drill press, engine lathe, vertical milling machine, horizontal milling machine, and the surface grinder. Introduces practical heat treatment of directly hardenable steels commonly used in machine shops. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices IV
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers practice in the operation of the drill press, engine lathe, vertical milling machine, horizontal milling machine, and the surface grinder. Introduces practical heat treatment of directly hardenable steels commonly used in machine shops. Part II of II.

courses.title: Machine Blueprint Reading I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces reading and interpreting blueprints and working drawings. Applies visualization of objects, sketching, and machine terminology. Part I of II.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Introduction to Algebra
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers topics in arithmetic through introduction to variables and equations.

courses.title: Learning Support for Quantitative Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 154
courses.description: Provides support to ensure success for students co-enrolled in Quantitative Reasoning (MTH 154). Course will review foundational topics through direct instruction, guided practice, and individualized support.

courses.title: Intermediate Algebra
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers topics in algebra.

courses.title: Learning Support for Pre-Calculus
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 161
courses.description: Provides support to ensure success for students co-enrolled in Pre-Calculus (MTH 161). Course will review foundational topics through direct instruction, guided practice, and individualized support.

courses.title: Phlebotomy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, components of health care delivery and clinical laboratory structure. Teaches techniques of specimen collection, specimen handling, and patient interactions.

courses.title: Clinical Phlebotomy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 8 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on obtaining blood specimens, processing specimens, managing assignments, assisting with and/or performing specified tests, performing clerical duties and maintaining professional communication. Provides supervised learning in college laboratory/and or cooperating agencies.

courses.title: Clinical Hematology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the cellular elements of blood including blood cell formation, and routine hematological procedures.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.
